Dates

Events

When a court or a committee sits, or rules, on police use of force, with the evidence record behind each date. This page lists when proceedings happen. What happened at an incident is on the incident pages.

Coming up and under way

Soonest first. Plans change, and a date in a news report can change within hours, so check the body's own notice before you travel. Where a report was corrected, the entry says so.

Past

Latest first.

What is listed here

Sittings of courts and of committees appointed by a court, and the dates of orders, where the proceeding concerns police use of force against protesters. Protests, marches and gatherings are recorded as incidents on their own pages.

An entry is listed once the archive holds a record of it. Each entry links to that evidence record, and its state is the record's state. A date reported by one outlet reads REPORTED. It reads VERIFIED only when the archive has read the court's or the committee's own document.

What it does not say

A hearing or a sitting on this list shows that a proceeding is happening. It does not show who authorised any force, and it does not show what a committee will find. The question of who gave the order stays on the incident pages, where each answer needs a document.

This page is in English only. If you know of a hearing or a sitting that is missing, send it with the notice or the report that gives the date.
